messages:
Lina (support): Heads-up — customer acme-inc reported repeated 429s this morning across their model route `/v1/generate/text` after a deploy window. They want a clear dashboard + alert we can point them to, and they want attribution: route vs model vs tenant. Can someone help triage?

Marco (eng-sre): On it. Do we have their tenant id or sample request ids? 429s could be quota exhaustion or our burst limiter.

Lina (support): Tenant id `acme-9942`. They pasted a sample response header: `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-ratelimit-reset: 167`. Also they see `quota_exceeded` in the body. Root cause unclear.

Priya (eng-platform): Ok first step: check our rate_limit telemetry for that tenant + route. I'll run the quick ClickHouse query to get 429 counts by (tenant,route,model) over the last 6h.

Priya (eng-platform): Query I ran:```sql
SELECT tenant_id, route, model_id, countIf(status=429) as cnt, count() as total
FROM requests_telemetry
WHERE tenant_id='acme-9942' AND timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 6 hour
GROUP BY tenant_id, route, model_id
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Priya (eng-platform): Results: 429s concentrated on `/v1/generate/text` for model `rwd-7b-quant` — 1.2k 429s in 20m window starting 1978000600. Other routes negligible.

Marco (eng-sre): That matches a burst fingerprint. Was there an autoscale/resize event around that time? SRE-Bot, any deployment noise?

SRE-Bot: auto-scaler: scaled_down pool-gpu-1 -> scaled_up pool-gpu-1 (burst) at 1978000589. No failed pods reported.

Marco (eng-sre): Interesting — autoscale churn might have tightened concurrency causing short-lived 429s. But Priya's data shows it looks like tenant-level quota exhausted (lots of 429s with x-ratelimit-remaining 0). We should confirm token-level vs tenant-level.

Alex (eng-ml): Also check model-side throughput limits — rwd-7b-quant has lower token/s limits. If many parallel short requests, batching may underutilize tokens and trigger tenant quota. We should correlate tokens generated per second vs quota windows.

Priya (eng-platform): I pulled token-usage series for tenant:```promql
sum(rate(tokens_generated_total{tenant_id="acme-9942",model="rwd-7b-quant"}[1m])) by (tenant_id)
```

Priya (eng-platform): Tokens spiked to ~420k tokens/min at the time. Their committed quota is 500k tokens/min burstable to 600k for 5m. So nominally within burst, but our per-route throttler also enforces a short-window smoothing that they hit.

Lina (support): Customer is asking: can we attribute the 429s to their traffic pattern vs our routing? They want to know if changing concurrency or adding retries would help.

Marco (eng-sre): Short answer: mostly tenant-side quota exhaustion on top of model throughput smoothing. Attribution breakdown I would use for the dashboard: 1) 429s by tenant, 2) 429s by route, 3) 429s by model_id, 4) token/sec vs quota windows. We have those metrics; just need to surface and add an alert.

Jess (product): For customer-facing docs, let's prepare a one-pager that explains signatures in response headers and recommends mitigation (client-side rate limit backoff, bundle smaller concurrent rate, use dedicated capacity).

Marco (eng-sre): Proposed Grafana panels: - Timeseries: 429 count (by tenant) - Heatmap: 429 rate across routes - Timeseries: tokens/sec vs quota limit line - Table: top request fingerprints (client tokens, route, model) - Alert: when 429_rate(tenant, 5m) > 10% of requests AND tokens/sec > 90% quota for 3m.

Priya (eng-platform): Alert rule (pseudo):```yaml
alert: TenantBurst429s
expr: (sum(rate(requests_total{tenant_id="$tenant",status=429}[5m])) by (tenant) / sum(rate(requests_total{tenant_id="$tenant"}[5m])) by (tenant)) > 0.10
AND
(sum(rate(tokens_generated_total{tenant_id="$tenant"}[5m])) by (tenant) / tenant_quota_tokens_per_5m{tenant="$tenant"}) > 0.90
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "High 429 rate for tenant {{ $labels.tenant }}"
  runbook: "/runbooks/observability/429-tenant-burst"
```

Alex (eng-ml): For attribution to model vs route: add labels to requests_telemetry for `model_id` and `route`; join on those and compute fractional share of 429s. If >80% tied to single model_id, flag model-saturation.

Lina (support): Can we give the customer an actionable repro + immediate mitigation they can do?

Marco (eng-sre): Yes: repro steps to show burst behavior:```bash
# single-tenant parallel burst (do not run against prod without throttling)
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/text &
done; wait
# check response headers for x-ratelimit-remaining and 429 responses
```

Marco (eng-sre): Immediate mitigations to recommend: 1) add client-side concurrency limit (e.g., max 20 concurrent requests), 2) exponential backoff on 429 with jitter, 3) if steady high QPS, consider Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.

Jess (product): I'll draft the customer-facing explanation and link to the dashboard + alert. Lina, can you send acme-inc the dashboard link + a short explanation of what we found and suggested mitigations?

Lina (support): Will do. Draft to send: "We observed a concentrated burst hitting your tenant quota window around 1978000600 causing short-lived 429s on /v1/generate/text for model rwd-7b-quant. Root cause: bursty parallel requests combined with model throughput smoothing. Mitigations: add client concurrency limit, exponential backoff on 429s, or upgrade to Dedicated. We've provisioned a Grafana panel and an alert — here is the link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/obs/tenant-429s?var-tenant=acme-9942" :thumbsup:

Marco (eng-sre): I'll also add a small sampling tracer to attach a request fingerprint (sha1 of normalized prompt + headers) to the 429 telemetry so future attribution by fingerprint is easier. Planning a small rollout tonight.

Priya (eng-platform): I put the new dashboard panels into the support dashboard folder and added the alert rule in staging. Will promote to prod after a 1h smoke.

Lina (support): Thanks all. Closing loop with customer now and will reopen if they see more 429s.

SRE-Bot: Incident note: created ticket RWD-INC-4321 for dashboard + sampling-tracer rollout.
